name: Fuzzing & Automated Testing
description: Fuzzing techniques, coverage-guided testing, and bug-finding pipelines.
narrative:
In 2018 the field was busy turning the raw idea of fuzzing into something rigorous and steerable. A foundational concern was simply doing the science right: "Evaluating Fuzz Testing" (CCS 2018) showed that many published gains evaporated under careful statistical comparison, setting evaluation norms the whole community would lean on. Alongside this, papers attacked the core weakness of random mutation — getting past hard checks in the code. "Angora: Efficient Fuzzing by Principled Search" (S&P 2018) used taint and gradient-style search to solve input constraints, "QSYM" (USENIX 2018) made concolic execution fast enough to pair with a fuzzer in true hybrid mode, and "T-Fuzz" (S&P 2018) simply transformed away the checks blocking coverage. Others refined coverage itself ("CollAFL", S&P 2018) or aimed fuzzing at specific targets ("Hawkeye", CCS 2018), while a parallel thread pushed fuzzing onto hard-to-reach platforms like IoT apps ("IoTFuzzer", NDSS 2018), embedded firmware ("What You Corrupt Is Not What You Crash", NDSS 2018), and OS kernels ("MoonShine", USENIX 2018).

2019 brought sharper tricks for the constraint and structure problems. "REDQUEEN" (NDSS 2019) exploited input-to-state correspondence to crack magic bytes and checksums almost for free, a result so cheap and effective it reshaped later fuzzers. For programs needing highly structured input, grammar-aware generation took hold with "NAUTILUS" (NDSS 2019) and, for JavaScript engines, "CodeAlchemist" (NDSS 2019). Machine learning entered seriously through "NEUZZ" (S&P 2019), which approximated program behavior with a neural net to guide mutation. The hybrid-fuzzing line matured with smarter scheduling ("Send Hardest Problems My Way", NDSS 2019), and fuzzing reached new bug classes and domains — kernel data races ("Razzer", S&P 2019) and IoT firmware at speed ("FIRM-AFL", USENIX 2019) — while "Full-Speed Fuzzing" (S&P 2019) cut instrumentation overhead and "ProFuzzer" (S&P 2019) probed input types on the fly.

By 2020 the work was about being smarter per execution and reaching deeper state. Data-flow guidance ("GREYONE", USENIX 2020) and bug-driven hybrid testing ("SAVIOR", S&P 2020) prioritized effort where bugs were likely; "Ijon" (S&P 2020) let humans annotate programs to escape deep state-space traps. Tooling broadened the reach of fuzzing: "RetroWrite" (S&P 2020) instrumented stripped binaries, "FuzzGen" (USENIX 2020) auto-generated library fuzzers, and firmware re-hosting ("HALucinator", USENIX 2020) plus kernel hybrid fuzzing ("HFL", NDSS 2020) opened systems software. Domain-specific validity feedback appeared for databases ("SQUIRREL", CCS 2020), efficiency was framed as a bandit problem ("EcoFuzz", USENIX 2020), and filesystem races got dedicated fuzzers ("Krace", S&P 2020).

The most recent stretch consolidates and specializes. Hardware joined the party with differential RTL fuzzing ("DifuzzRTL", S&P 2021), directed fuzzing gained provable guarantees ("BEACON", S&P 2022), and IoT firmware testing went black-box via message inference ("Snipuzz", CCS 2021). Crucially, "LibAFL" (CCS 2022) turned the field's accumulated tricks into a modular, reusable framework rather than one-off forks. Most recently, large language models entered as a generator of structured inputs, with "Large Language Model guided Protocol Fuzzing" (NDSS 2024) using an LLM to fuzz protocols that lack any machine-readable specification — signaling where the area is heading next.

milestones.title: QSYM : A Practical Concolic Execution Engine Tailored for Hybrid Fuzzing
milestones.note: made concolic execution fast enough to make hybrid fuzzing practical

milestones.title: REDQUEEN: Fuzzing with Input-to-State Correspondence
milestones.note: cracked magic bytes and checksums cheaply via input-to-state correspondence

milestones.title: NEUZZ: Efficient Fuzzing with Neural Program Smoothing
milestones.note: brought neural models in to guide mutation, opening the ML-for-fuzzing thread

milestones.title: GREYONE: Data Flow Sensitive Fuzzing
milestones.note: used data-flow sensitivity to steer mutation toward hard-to-reach code

milestones.title: Ijon: Exploring Deep State Spaces via Fuzzing
milestones.note: introduced human annotations to escape deep state-space traps fuzzers could not reach
